latin: Lonicera ligustrina var. yunnanensis PURPLE STORM ('Grln02')
hardinessNote: Hardy through a very cold UK winter, approximately -20 to -15°C.
visual: Dense glossy evergreen with dark purple new shoots · a disease-free box alternative
soilWarning: Purple shoots colour best in sun
water: Water regularly in its first year; tolerates dry spells once settled.
prune: Clip to shape two or three times in the growing season; tolerates hard cutting back.
toxicity: Berries should not be eaten; they may cause a stomach upset in children and pets.
compliance: Protected by plant breeders' rights (EU PVR, US PP33761); propagation for sale needs a licence.
cvs: GREEN BREEZE ('Grln01') – bright green · COPPER GLOW ('Grln03') – copper-orange new shoots · 'Baggesen's Gold' – golden leaves, much larger
resilience: Tough, clip-tolerant and disease-free; copes with sun or shade and winter cold.
uses: Low hedging · topiary balls · box replacement · patio pots
foliage: evergreen; tiny glossy dark green leaves, purple when young
uncertain: hardiness: no RHS H-rating found in search; Sapho gives hardy to -18°C (H6 band) and the deck's sibling L. ligustrina 'Baggesen's Gold' is H6
height/spread: 90 × 60 cm is the RHS 'in three years' figure; ultimate size not published, Sunset gives 2–3 ft
compliance: EU PVR number differs between sources (Kernock 61434, Sapho 61435), so no number given
naming: RHS uses L. ligustrina var. yunnanensis; trade still sells it as L. nitida; Forge label read 'Semptations Garden Clouds Purple Storm'
peak: sold for year-round foliage; purple shoots strongest in spring
clay: not stated by any source
ratings: from RHS/nursery descriptions (disease-free, sun or shade) and the sibling card, not measured
